01 / THE MECHANISM

An answer should
stand up to a challenge.

Smart contracts need a way to learn what happened outside the chain. Lituus proposes an open process: stake on an answer, allow time to dispute it, then resolve.

[ 01 ]

Open participation.

Ask, report or challenge. The proposed mechanism does not require a committee’s permission.

[ 02 ]

Skin in the game.

Answers carry REP bonds. Backing an answer that loses can cost the stake behind it.

[ 03 ]

A way through disputes.

Challenges increase the stakes. A fork is the last resort when earlier rounds cannot settle a dispute.

THE STAKE BEHIND THE ANSWER

Reputation.
With something
at stake.

REP is the participation token behind Augur’s oracle. In the Lituus design, it funds questions and backs reported answers.

Participation carries responsibility. Bonds can be lost, and REP holders need to pay attention to forks.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

Start
here.

All questions ↗
Is Augur Lituus live?+

Augur Lituus is in development. The whitepaper and implementation are public. This page’s interactive example is educational and does not connect to a deployed oracle.

Is Augur a prediction market or an oracle?+

Augur’s original platform combined prediction markets with a decentralized oracle. Lituus focuses on the oracle: a resolution layer designed for prediction markets and other applications.

What if people disagree about an answer?+

In the proposed Lituus design, anyone can challenge an answer by posting a larger REP bond. If disputes escalate far enough, a fork lets REP holders choose between outcome universes. Read the whitepaper for the full rules and assumptions.

What should REP holders know?+

REP is not a passive staking product. Reporting bonds can be lost, and holders need to monitor forks. The 2026 Moon Fork migration window is closed. Consult the current official guidance for REPv2_Yes_1.
